lines.say: This week, Washington warned Venezuela's leaders it could use force to stop the drug trade.
But in 1989, America sent troops into Panama to seize a leader charged with drug trafficking.
Manuel Noriega ruled Panama as its military strongman. In 1988, a US court charged him with drug trafficking.
By the end of 1989, he had militias of his own, the Dignity Battalions.
On December 20th, President George H. W. Bush ordered the invasion.
Paratroopers dropped into Panama in the middle of the night.
Fighting burned parts of Panama City. The number of dead is still disputed.
On January 3rd, Noriega surrendered and was flown to Florida to face trial.
A US court convicted him of drug trafficking.
Now the same threat hangs over Venezuela.
Should one country be able to remove another country's leader by force?
